source.title: Enabling Agents to Communicate Entirely in Latent Space
source.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2026, Long Papers)

confidence_rationale: Peer-reviewed (ACL 2026 long paper, DOI verified on the ACL Anthology; arXiv 2511.09149 v4 read for method detail). The thought's description is accurate: last-layer hidden states are passed as the message, injected into the receiver's input-embedding sequence through a trained light-weight self-attention plus projection adapter, with full SFT on Qwen2.5-7B/0.5B and LLaMA3.1-8B base models and a token-to-latent replacement curriculum. The one result that bears on ARC-139 is the heterogeneous pair: a Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct sender feeding a LLaMA3.1-8B-Base actor reached 71.39% unseen accuracy against a 57.46% baseline -- integration across two differently-trained representational spaces through a trained low-complexity adapter, with no attempt to make the two models' representations the same. The paper also reports content-specificity ablations (cross-task latents, covariance-matched Gaussian and random-rotation surrogates degrade performance); I could not cleanly verify the CrossTask figures from the HTML extraction and have not relied on them. Held at 0.5: LLM agents on ALFWorld and MATH, trained adapter, and it is feasibility evidence, not a test of specialisation and legibility rising together.
failure_signatures: If ARC-139 is right, heterogeneous systems should be bridgeable by a LOW-complexity trained map without representational convergence; Interlat's adapter is small but the sender and actor are ALSO fully fine-tuned, so the result does not isolate the bridge from co-adaptation of the endpoints -- a REE replication with FROZEN endpoints (MECH-538's protocol) could come out differently.

The content-specificity ablations are reported but the extracted CrossTask numbers (61.19% vs 61.43%) do not read as a drop; treat Interlat as feasibility evidence and rely on Cheng/Das/Ramnath and Zhang/Emu for the example-specificity question.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Interlat transmits an LLM agent's last-layer hidden states directly as its message, consumed by another agent through a trained light-weight adapter, and outperforms fine-tuned chain-of-thought and single-agent baselines 'even across heterogeneous models'; a separate latent-space reasoner compresses messages for up to 24x lower latency. Ablations with cross-task, Gaussian-surrogate and randomly-rotated messages indicate the actor is sensitive to the message's specific geometry.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-139 asserts that integration does not require representational sameness. Interlat's heterogeneous Qwen->LLaMA result is an existence proof in the ML domain: two independently pretrained representational spaces coordinated through a small trained interface, with the sender's private representation left as it is.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Both endpoints are fine-tuned alongside the adapter, so this is not the frozen-endpoint, minimum-bridge measurement MECH-538 specifies and cannot show that the bridge alone carried the integration. Two-agent LLM setting on one embodied benchmark (ALFWorld) and one symbolic one (MATH); the authors list scale, closed-model inaccessibility and interpretability loss as limitations. Says nothing about local specialisation rising with legibility, which is ARC-139's non-redundant prediction.
mapping.source_context: LLM multi-agent; Qwen2.5-7B/0.5B-Base, LLaMA3.1-8B-Base, cross-family sender/actor pair; ALFWorld and MATH.

confidence_components.notes: Top NLP venue; full SFT of both endpoints weakens it as bridge evidence. Transfer risk high: LLM agents exchanging reasoning traces are not E1/E2 in an embodied forward model.
